title: Ask is Command K on videos as well as pictures, and its sheen plays on every hover
goal: Two fixes to the Ask button. First, Command K opens Ask everywhere, on a video as well as a picture, and the button shows the key in both. Today a video gives Command K to splitting a clip at the playhead instead. Second, the light sheen that sweeps across the Ask button when the pointer arrives plays every time the pointer comes back, not only the first time.
notes:
The user, 2026-10-24: 'make sure that ask button has the same keystroke (cmd-k) on both image and video!. Also, when I hover over it the first time it has a nice sheen animation, but subsequent hovers do not repeat the sheen'.

The sheen is a miss on the just-shipped task the-ask-button-is-the-design-s-hero-button-a-vio (done 2026-10-24, commit 224236f2), whose acceptance said one sweep per hover.

Sheen SUSPECT, not reproduced: Sources/Photonz/DesignSystem/HeroButtonStyle.swift ~145 drives the band with .keyframeAnimator(initialValue: 0.0, trigger: sweeps) and a single LinearKeyframe(HeroSheen.duration). On a new trigger a keyframe animator starts from its CURRENT value, which after the first sweep is already HeroSheen.duration, so the second run animates duration to duration and nothing moves. A MoveKeyframe(0) first in the track is the likely fix. Other suspect: the ButtonStyle body's @State (hovering, sweeps) being reset or the hover callback not firing again; check onHover actually fires on re-entry (it is wrapped by playtestHover, Sources/Photonz/Playtest/PlaytestPointer.swift:94). Reproduce before fixing.

Command K: Sources/Photonz/EditorCommands.swift:524-533 (Ask item, keyboardShortcut nil when timed) and :789-795 (Split at Playhead takes Command K on the timeline, B off it); Sources/Photonz/Agent/AskViews.swift:65,69 hide the key on a video. docs/design/mocks/shared/UX-PATTERNS.md:2134 lists '⌘K split' among the video keys and must be updated; also the earlier task on-a-video-the-ask-button-never-sits-on-top-of-t. The user's explicit request overrides Premiere parity for this one key.
acceptance: On a video at Next defaults Command K opens Ask, the title bar button shows the key as it does on a picture, and its tooltip names it; the Edit menu's Ask item carries Command K in both

Split at Playhead moves to another key that conflicts with nothing in the video editor's menus or the timeline's single-key tools; the runner picks it from what Premiere or Final Cut give the same command, checks every shortcut in the app for a clash (a test lists them), and writes the choice and why in docs/design and the task log; the timeline's own K without Command (shuttle) is untouched
Reproduced first: hover the Ask button, leave, hover again; the second and later hovers show no sweep today. Recorded in the log before fixing

After the fix, every fresh arrival of the pointer sweeps the sheen once (tested at least five times in a row, including arriving again before the previous sweep finished), it still does not repeat while the pointer stays, and Reduce Motion still skips it
A reel under queue/audits/ shows three hovers in a row each sweeping, with a contact sheet; the frames prove the band crosses the button on the third hover
Walks that press Command K on a video, or expect Split at Playhead on it, are updated and pass (Scripts/playtest-all.sh --no-build on the touched walks)
Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not

log.note: Reproduced before fixing: new walk Scripts/playtest/ask-sheen-every-hover-walk.json films the Ask button (new filmHover step, ScreenCaptureKit at display rate) through three hovers with the pointer leaving between. Hover 1: a white band crosses left to right (frames 263ms..530ms). Hovers 2 and 3: no band in any frame, only the pink end of the spectrum fading in. Contact sheet looked at by eye (/tmp/hover-compare.png). Matches the suspect: the keyframe animator restarts from its current value, already at the end of the sweep.

owns these walks: ask-is-command-k-on-a-video-walk, ask-sheen-every-hover-walk, ask-hero-button-walk, premiere-keys-on-the-timeline-walk, timeline-right-click-menus-walk, tutorial-cut-a-recording-down-walk

Adversarial pass before building: a Premiere editor loses Command K for Add Edit, so the cut needs a key they would also know; Final Cut's Blade is Command B and nothing in the video editor's menus or the timeline's key map uses it (B alone stays the Blade tool, plain K stays shuttle stop). Photoshop's Command B (Color Balance) is a picture command and not built here. Chose Command B over Shift Command K-style moves because it is the other grown-up video tool's key for the same command (UX-PATTERNS 7). Chose to keep Split Everything on Premiere's Shift Command K over moving it to Shift Command B, because Ask does not want it and Shift Command B is Blur Behind Selection on a picture.

Sheen fix: the keyframe track now starts with MoveKeyframe(0), the band is parked at the end at rest, and a transaction keeps the face's hover animation off the band (Sources/Photonz/DesignSystem/HeroButtonStyle.swift). Which arrivals sweep is HeroSheen.sweeps in PhotonzCore, unit tested with Reduce Motion and a dimmed button. New walk step filmHover (PlaytestHoverFilm, SheenSweep, docs/design/playtest-harness.md) films a control while the pointer arrives. After the fix the walk claims a sweep on hovers 1, 2, 3, 5 (arriving mid sweep of 4) and 6, and none while the pointer stays: all pass. Looked at the contact sheet: the band crosses on the third hover as on the first.

Command K: Ask's Edit menu row and the title bar button carry Command K on a video; the timeline key map (TimelineKeys) gives Command B to Split at Playhead and leaves Command K to the menu. Menu bar read on a video with the probe in front (ask-is-command-k-on-a-video-walk, menus oneKeyEach): Ask ⌘K, Split at Playhead ⌘B, Split Everything ⇧⌘K, no live clash. 30 walks that pressed Command K to cut now press Command B; all 35 touched walks plus the two new ones pass. Docs: UX-PATTERNS 7 and the timeline keys list, video.md, ask.md, tutorials.md, timeline-right-click.md, video-vs-premiere.md.

left rough: the menu reading on a video prints ⌫ on two dimmed rows, Clip > Delete This Piece and Sequence > Track > Delete Track (menus-1-video-keys.txt). Neither is live at the same time and it was there before this task, so it did not earn its own task; noted here for a later pass on the menus.

Command K opens Ask on a video as on a picture; the button and its tooltip show the key in both, and the Edit menu's Ask row carries it. Split at Playhead moved to Command B (Final Cut's Blade), with no menu clash on a video (menus oneKeyEach, probe in front). The sheen sweeps on every arrival: reproduced first on film (hovers 2 and 3 drew no band), fixed with a MoveKeyframe back to the start, proven over six filmed hovers including one mid sweep, none while staying; Reduce Motion rule unit tested. New filmHover walk step. 35 touched walks plus 2 new pass; Scripts/test.sh green (14444 tests). Commit 69d1a7a9. Audit queue/audits/2026-10-24-ask-is-command-k-on-videos-as-well-as-pictures-a.json with reel and contact sheet.

Note: commit 69d1a7a9 also carried one line of the user's own uncommitted edit in docs/design/tutorials.md (walk set 'about 910 walks and about 245 minutes' -> 'about 1010 walks and about 290 minutes'), the same count update sitting uncommitted in CLAUDE.md and the queue docs.
